title: Meta's Muse can shop and check out for you. Here's how it works
source_used: BigGo Finance (4 Oct 2026) and Fox News (3 Oct 2026); CNBC original blocked (403), Crypto Briefing and Traders Union also blocked
key_facts: Meta's personal AI agent Muse, launched 8 Sep 2026, browses, fills forms, compares prices and completes purchases, pausing for user approval before payments.
Stripe's agent wallet Link was the first payment method; Shopify's Shop Pay was announced as a supported wallet in Muse on 23 Sep 2026, giving Muse access to Shopify stores.
At Meta Connect 2026 on 23 Sep, Meta said Walmart, Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Ulta and Wayfair would be added as Muse-supported retailers.
Amazon has blocked Muse from searching and buying on Amazon.com and asked Meta to restrict it, citing terms that require AI agents to identify themselves.
Sensor Tower: Muse passed 5 million US downloads within 22 days of launch; Fox News cited reports of more than 3 million by late September.
For purchases, Meta says Link can generate a one-time card number so the merchant and the agent never see the user's real card.
CNBC's 3 Oct piece is an explainer of how this checkout works; the Crypto Briefing and Traders Union headlines of 3 Oct mention checkout fees and retail partnerships, which could not be read.
quote_evidence: Shopify has fully opened its stores to Muse and integrated Shop Pay checkout, while Amazon has blocked Muse's access to its platform.
Two days later, on the 23rd, Shop Pay was officially announced as a supported wallet within Muse.
For purchases, Meta says Link can generate a one-time card number at checkout.
why_it_matters_hint: Agent shopping is now live for Meta's millions of Muse users, and retailers are splitting between opening up (Shopify) and blocking (Amazon).
event_date: 8 Sep 2026 launch; 23 Sep 2026 Shop Pay and retail partners; CNBC explainer 3 Oct 2026
notes: CNBC blocked (403). Written from BigGo Finance (own compilation) and Fox News; two 3 Oct outlets mentioning possible checkout fees were blocked, so that detail is not confirmed. Underlying capability dates from September, so this is a follow-up rather than new news.
